unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Printing from Your Computer
drDigitalIntro:
Printing puts what is on your screen onto paper — and one shortcut opens the Print window almost anywhere.
• The shortcut is Ctrl+P. On a Mac it is Command+P. P for Print.
• The Print window shows a preview, lets you pick a printer, and choose how many copies.
• No printer? The same window can save the page as a PDF instead — pick 'Save as PDF' where the printer name goes.
• The common mistake: hunting through menus for a Print button. The shortcut works even when there is no button.
• Prove it to me below — this page can tell when you really press it.

playgroundTask.goal: You know the shortcut that prints from almost any program

steps.say: Press Ctrl+P right now (Command+P on a Mac).
steps.detail: Press it while you are on this page. I will catch it before the Print window opens — this one is just practice.

steps.say: Now do it for real: open any web page you like in another tab and press the same shortcut there.
steps.detail: A recipe, an article, anything. The Print window will appear with a preview. Look at the printer choice — see 'Save as PDF' in the list? Then press Cancel (or print it, if you have a printer and want to!).

drDigitalSuccess: That shortcut works in nearly every program you will ever use. You can put anything on paper now — or save it as a PDF when there is no printer around.
drDigitalHint: Hold the Ctrl key (or Command on a Mac) and tap the letter P once.
